'''''Yucca flaccida''''', commonly called '''Adam's needle'''<ref name=FNA/> or '''weak-leaf yucca''',<ref name=USDA/> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the asparagus [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] ([[Asparagaceae]]). It is [[native plant|native]] to south-central and southeastern North America, from the lower Great Plains eastward to the Atlantic seaboard in [[Virginia]], south through [[Florida]] and the Gulf states.<ref name=Kew/> Its natural habitat is in sandy open woodlands and fields.<ref name=FNA/> It is not considered to be threatened by the [[IUCN]].<ref name="iucn status 19 November 2021" />

==Description==
It is a stemless [[evergreen]] [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|55|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|150|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad. It has a basal rosette of sharply pointed, swordlike leaves up to {{convert|55|cm|0|abbr=on}} long. In summer, {{convert|150|cm|0|abbr=on}} long panicles of bell-shaped creamy white flowers are held above the foliage.<ref name=RHSAZ/>

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''flaccida'' means "weak", "feeble", referring to the leaves which often fold under their own weight (the inner leaves may remain erect as they are supported by the outer ones).<ref name=RHSLG/>

==Taxonomy==
Some authorities regard ''Y. flaccida'' as a [[variety (botany)|variety]] or [[form (botany)|form]] of ''[[Yucca filamentosa|Y. filamentosa]]'', rather than as a separate species.<ref name=FNA/>

Populations in the [[South Central United States|South Central Region]] of the United States with unusually narrow leaves have been segregated as ''Y. louisianensis'' by some authorities.<ref name=Weakley/><ref name=tx/> This entity is found in the states of Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, and Texas.<ref name=BONAP2/>

==Ecology==
A number of yucca moths lay their eggs upon ''Y. flaccida'' as a host plant, an example being ''[[Tegeticula intermedia]]''.<ref name=tolweb/>

==Cultivation==
It is cultivated and valued as an architectural plant.<ref name=RHSAZ /> Numerous [[cultivars]] are available, some with variegated leaves, of which 'Golden Sword'<ref name=RHS3/> and 'Ivory'<ref name=RHS2/> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHS/>
